readme: mic-trigger — clap, tap or sing into the mic; each onset plays a random
note of the scale. Four ordinary objects, each doing one thing:
mic (audioin track, monitor off)
-> onset (loudness source=mic): fires when the level crosses threshold
-> notes (randomnotes trigger=onset): one random degree per firing
--notes--> pluck (karplus) --> verb --> master
onset also strikes 'toss' (modlfo sh strike=onset) --> pluck.pan,
so every hit lands somewhere new in the stereo field.
The browser asks for the microphone once. Use headphones, or keep
/mic monitor=off (the default here) — the mic isn't heard, only analysed.
Try:
/start
/onset threshold=-40         more sensitive (dBFS); -20 = only loud hits
/onset hold=0.25             at most one firing per 0.25s
/notes scale=0,2,4           which scale degrees it picks from
/notes probability=0.5       skip half the hits
/harmony root=55             retune everything it plays
/mic monitor=on              hear the mic through the track (fx, sends)
/mic device=scarlett channels=2   another input, e.g. interface input 2
/onset mode=envelope         its signal outlet becomes the level itself —
patch it into any param to follow your voice
Several outputs (e.g. a Scarlett with outs 3-4):
/devices                     list devices
/master device=scarlett      play through it
/add_output name=phones channels=3,4
/verb add_send=phones        the reverb on 3-4 too; /outputs lists routing
